extracted.intended_audience: PR students, interns, and early-career public relations practitioners learning to write press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a standard news/press release with correct structure, required elements, AP-style date line formatting, and paragraph organization aimed at students and new PR practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo placement and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The logo should be located at the top and center of your press release. Use the logo of the company or organization you are writing about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the organization's official logo prominently at the top center so recipients can immediately identify the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information content and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your contact information should be left-aligned below the image of the logo. The contact information should consist of your name, job title, phone number and email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a single clear contact block (name, title, phone, email) left-aligned beneath the logo so journalists know whom to reach for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline clarity and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The headline is located centered underneath the contact information. The headline should allow the reader to know instantly what the press release is about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a concise, informative headline and center it beneath the contact block so the main news is immediately obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date line format and AP Style
rubrics_metrics.description: The date line is left-aligned below the headline. It typically includes the city, state and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to AP Style rules in this section: make sure the city is in ALL CAPS, abbreviate the state as needed, and abbreviate the date as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate placement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: After you have written your press release, you will typically skip a couple of lines, insert “###” centered, skip a couple more lines and insert the boilerplate. The boilerplate is typically three or four sentences consisting of the company name, headquarters, founding and accolades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a centered '###' marker before the boilerplate; keep the boilerplate short (3–4 sentences) summarizing the organization's basic facts and credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footer content
rubrics_metrics.description: The footer should be the last item on your press release. The footer should include the company mailing address, phone number, website and social media outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude with complete contact/follow information (mailing address, phone, website, social links) as the final element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall paragraph structure (three core paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases typically consist of three core paragraphs but can certainly have more if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use three main paragraphs as a standard structure, expanding if the story requires additional detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 1: nut graph and essential facts
rubrics_metrics.description: This paragraph typically consists of the date line (as mentioned in the section above) along with the nut graph. Here you will find the who, what, when and where pieces of information about the news. This paragraph is typically three or four sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the nut graph: succinctly answer who, what, when and where in 3–4 sentences to give journalists the core facts immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 2: supporting details for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: This paragraph includes side information or fill-in details that are helpful to a journalist. This paragraph is often two to four sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide background, context, statistics, or other supporting details that help reporters flesh out the story; keep it concise (2–4 sentences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 3: quotes placement
rubrics_metrics.description: This paragraph consists of quotes. Quotes should begin the first sentence of the third paragraph because journalists will quickly see the quotation marks, in case they need context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the third paragraph with a quoted statement (quotation marks) so journalists can quickly identify a spokesperson's quote and use it for context or attribution.
